title: Dumlao v. COMELEC
summary: The Supreme Court declared unconstitutional the provision of BP 52 that imposed an additional qualification for candidates based on age (mandatory retirement), as it violated the equal protection clause by creating an irrational classification among elective officials.
doctrine: Additional qualifications for candidates for local elective positions beyond those prescribed by the Constitution and the Local Government Code violate the equal protection clause when they create unreasonable classifications. The legislature cannot impose qualifications that are not germane to the purpose of the law.
fullText:
MELENCIO-HERRERA, J.:

The constitutionality of the first paragraph of Section 4 of Batas Pambansa Blg. 52, which provides for an additional disqualification for elective local officials, is challenged in this case.

The provision disqualifies any retired elective provincial, city, or municipal official who has received retirement benefits and who is 65 years of age at the commencement of the term of office. The petitioner argues that this provision violates the equal protection clause.

The equal protection clause does not require universal applicability of laws. Classification is permissible provided it is based on substantial distinctions, is germane to the purpose of the law, applies to future conditions, and applies equally to all members of the same class. The classification in this case fails the test of reasonableness.
